nodes.label: Claude Code hooks
nodes.rationale: Hooks are user-defined shell commands, HTTP endpoints, MCP tool calls, LLM prompts, or agents that execute automatically at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle. They run wherever Claude Code runs: terminal, IDE extensions, Desktop app, and Claude Code on the web all fire the same hook events.

nodes.label: Hook lifecycle cadences
nodes.rationale: Events fall into three cadences: once per session (SessionStart, SessionEnd), once per turn (UserPromptSubmit, Stop, StopFailure), and on every tool call inside the agentic loop (PreToolUse, PostToolUse) — except EndConversation calls, which skip both tool events.

nodes.label: Hook configuration schema
nodes.rationale: Hooks are defined in JSON settings files with three nesting levels: choose a hook event, add a matcher group to filter when it fires, and define one or more hook handlers to run when matched.

nodes.label: Matcher patterns
nodes.rationale: The matcher field filters when hooks fire: '*'/empty matches all; strings of only letters, digits, _, -, spaces, ',' and '|' are exact strings or separated lists; any other character makes it an unanchored JavaScript regex (Edit.* matches NotebookEdit — anchor ^...$ for whole-string). Each event matches on a different field (tool name, session source, agent type, error type...), and several events support no matcher at all. Hyphen exact-match needs v2.1.195+, comma separators v2.1.191+.

nodes.label: if field (permission-rule filter)
nodes.rationale: Optional per-handler filter using permission rule syntax (Bash(git *), Edit(*.ts)); holds exactly ONE rule and is evaluated only on tool events. For Bash it checks each subcommand including inside $() and backticks, strips leading VAR=value assignments, and FAILS OPEN when the command can't be parsed — best-effort only, so hard allow/deny belongs in the permission system, not a hook.

nodes.label: Hook handler
nodes.rationale: The shell command, HTTP endpoint, MCP tool, LLM prompt, or agent that runs when a matcher matches — five types: command, http, mcp_tool, prompt, agent. All matching hooks run in parallel; the same handler defined in more than one settings file runs once, but a plugin's or skill's copy stays separate.

nodes.label: Command hook (type: command)
nodes.rationale: Runs a shell command with JSON input on stdin and results via exit codes and stdout. Runs with the user's full permissions, and since v2.1.139 in its own session without a controlling terminal, so it cannot open /dev/tty or write escape sequences directly to the interface.

nodes.label: HTTP hook (type: http)
nodes.rationale: POSTs the event JSON to a URL with Content-Type application/json; the response body uses the same JSON output schema as command hooks. Non-2xx responses, connection failures, and timeouts are all NON-blocking — to block or deny, the endpoint must return 2xx with a JSON decision body.

nodes.label: MCP tool hook (type: mcp_tool)
nodes.rationale: Calls a tool on an already-connected MCP server (never triggers an OAuth or connection flow); the tool's text output is treated like command-hook stdout. SessionStart and Setup typically fire before servers finish connecting, so hooks there should expect a 'not connected' error on first run.

nodes.label: Prompt-based hook (type: prompt)
nodes.rationale: Sends the hook input plus a prompt (with $ARGUMENTS placeholder) to a fast Claude model for single-turn evaluation; the model returns {ok, reason} and ok:false becomes decision 'block'. continueOnBlock feeds the reason back to Claude and continues the turn instead of ending it, on events that support it; default timeout 30s.

nodes.label: Agent-based hook (type: agent)
nodes.rationale: Experimental: spawns a subagent that can use tools like Read, Grep, and Glob for up to 50 turns before returning the same {ok, reason} schema as prompt hooks; default timeout 60s. Useful when verification requires inspecting actual files or test output rather than only the hook input.

nodes.label: Exec form (args present)
nodes.rationale: When args is set, command is resolved as an executable on PATH and spawned directly with args as the argument vector — no shell, no tokenization on any platform, placeholders substituted as plain strings. Required for path placeholders; on Windows the command must be a real executable (.cmd/.bat shims can't be spawned — invoke the underlying script with node instead).

nodes.label: Shell form (args absent)
nodes.rationale: When args is omitted, the command string is passed to a shell (sh -c on macOS/Linux; Git Bash on Windows, or PowerShell when Git Bash isn't installed) which tokenizes, expands variables, and interprets pipes, &&, redirects, and globs. Placeholders must be double-quoted here.

nodes.label: Hook timeout defaults
nodes.rationale: Per-hook timeout defaults: 600s for command/http/mcp_tool, 30s for prompt, 60s for agent. UserPromptSubmit lowers the command/http/mcp_tool default to 30s and MessageDisplay lowers it to 10s; async hooks use the same 10-minute default unless set.

nodes.label: SessionEnd shared 1.5s hook budget
nodes.rationale: SessionEnd hooks share a 1.5-second overall budget, applying to session exit, /clear, and switching sessions via interactive /resume. The budget is automatically raised to the highest per-hook timeout configured in settings files, up to 60 seconds.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS
nodes.rationale: The CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable explicitly overrides the SessionEnd shared hook budget, in milliseconds — e.g. CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 claude.

nodes.label: Plugin hook timeouts don't raise SessionEnd budget
nodes.rationale: Only per-hook timeouts set in settings files raise the SessionEnd shared budget; timeouts set on plugin-provided hooks do NOT raise it, so a slow plugin SessionEnd hook can still be cut off at the default 1.5s unless the env var or a settings-file timeout intervenes.

nodes.label: PermissionRequest headless default-deny
nodes.rationale: In sessions that can't show a permission prompt — such as background subagents in non-interactive mode — Claude Code still runs PermissionRequest hooks, and if no hook returns a decision, it DENIES the tool call.

nodes.label: Hook locations and scope
nodes.rationale: Where a hook is defined determines scope: ~/.claude/settings.json (all projects), .claude/settings.json (project, committable), .claude/settings.local.json (gitignored), managed policy settings, plugin hooks/hooks.json, and skill/agent frontmatter. Entries MERGE across levels rather than replacing; cloud sessions on Claude Code on the web don't read local ~/.claude/settings.json; settings/policy/plugin hooks also run inside subagents.

nodes.label: allowManagedHooksOnly
nodes.rationale: Enterprise administrators can set allowManagedHooksOnly to block user, project, and plugin hooks; hooks from plugins force-enabled in managed enabledPlugins are exempt, so vetted hooks can be distributed through an organization marketplace. Similarly, disableAllHooks set outside managed settings can never disable managed hooks.

nodes.label: HTTP hook allowlists
nodes.rationale: allowedHttpHookUrls (an HTTP hook runs only if its URL matches the merged allowlist) and httpHookAllowedEnvVars (only listed environment variables are interpolated into hook headers) apply to hooks from every source, including managed policy settings.

nodes.label: Exit code semantics
nodes.rationale: Exit 0 = success (stdout parsed for JSON); exit 2 = blocking error (stderr fed to Claude, stdout/JSON ignored); any other code = non-blocking error — exit 1 does NOT block despite being the conventional Unix failure code. Whether exit 2 actually blocks depends on the event: PreToolUse blocks the call, PostToolUse only shows stderr (tool already ran), StopFailure ignores everything, and WorktreeCreate uniquely fails on ANY non-zero exit.

nodes.label: JSON output fields
nodes.rationale: Exit 0 plus a JSON object on stdout gives finer control than exit codes: universal fields (continue:false stops Claude entirely and takes precedence over event decisions, stopReason, suppressOutput, systemMessage, terminalSequence), top-level decision/reason, and nested hookSpecificOutput requiring hookEventName. Output strings are capped at 10,000 characters (overflow saved to a file with a preview); JSON is only processed on exit 0 — choose exit-code signaling OR JSON, never both.

nodes.label: Per-event decision control patterns
nodes.rationale: Which events can block or steer behavior varies: top-level decision 'block' (UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, ConfigChange, PreCompact...), hookSpecificOutput patterns (PreToolUse permissionDecision, PermissionRequest decision.behavior, PermissionDenied retry, Elicitation action, MessageDisplay displayContent), path return (WorktreeCreate), context-only (SessionStart, Setup, SubagentStart), or none (Notification, SessionEnd, FileChanged, StopFailure...). A few events can also REWRITE content: PreToolUse updatedInput, PermissionRequest decision.updatedInput, PostToolUse updatedToolOutput; UserPromptSubmit can never replace the prompt.

nodes.label: permissionDecision (allow/deny/ask/defer)
nodes.rationale: PreToolUse's hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision has four outcomes: allow (skips the prompt, except for tools requiring user interaction), deny (blocks; reason shown to Claude), ask (forces a prompt — since v2.1.211 the auto-mode classifier can still deny but can no longer silently approve), and defer. Multi-hook precedence is deny > defer > ask > allow, and deny/ask permission rules are still evaluated regardless of the hook's answer. The old top-level decision approve/block is deprecated for this event.

nodes.label: defer / deferred tool call
nodes.rationale: permissionDecision 'defer' is honored only in non-interactive (-p) mode: the process exits with stop_reason 'tool_deferred' and the pending call preserved, the wrapper collects input (typically AskUserQuestion answers), resumes with claude -p --resume, and the hook then returns allow with updatedInput. It works only when Claude made a single tool call in the turn; interactive sessions log a warning and ignore it; resume restores the prior permission mode except plan and bypassPermissions.

nodes.label: updatedInput
nodes.rationale: Replaces a tool's ENTIRE input object before execution, so unchanged fields must be included. PreToolUse combines it with allow/ask; PermissionRequest carries it inside the decision object where the modified input is re-evaluated against deny/ask rules. It is also the only way to auto-approve AskUserQuestion or ExitPlanMode in headless mode — 'allow' alone is insufficient for tools requiring user interaction.

nodes.label: updatedToolOutput
nodes.rationale: PostToolUse's updatedToolOutput replaces the tool result before Claude sees it — but the tool has already run, so files written, commands executed, and telemetry all keep the original. The replacement must match the tool's output shape (e.g. Bash's {stdout, stderr, interrupted, isImage}); a non-conforming value for a built-in tool is ignored, while MCP tool output passes through unvalidated.

nodes.label: additionalContext
nodes.rationale: hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext injects a string into Claude's context as a system reminder at an event-specific position (session start, alongside the prompt, next to the tool result, or end of turn). Values over 10,000 chars go to a file with a preview; on --resume the saved text is REPLAYED rather than re-running the hook, so timestamps/SHAs go stale. Write factual statements — imperative out-of-band phrasing can trigger Claude's prompt-injection defenses.

nodes.label: terminalSequence
nodes.rationale: Because hooks run without a controlling terminal, terminalSequence (v2.1.141+) lets a hook return an escape sequence for Claude Code to emit through its own terminal write path — allowlisted to OSC 0/1/2 (titles), OSC 9/99/777 (notifications), and bare BEL. Anything outside the allowlist (CSI cursor/color, OSC 8 hyperlinks, OSC 52 clipboard, OSC 1337) causes the whole field to be ignored, so a hook can never corrupt the on-screen prompt.

nodes.label: Async hooks
nodes.rationale: async:true runs a command hook in the background without blocking Claude; decision fields have no effect because the action already proceeded. JSON output (additionalContext to Claude, systemMessage to the user) is delivered on the next conversation turn; asyncRewake additionally wakes Claude on exit 2 even when idle. claude -p kills still-running async hooks at teardown (outcome 'cancelled'); before v2.1.202 malformed async JSON could crash the session, recurring on every resume.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_ENV_FILE
nodes.rationale: The CLAUDE_ENV_FILE environment variable names a file where a hook can append export statements; variables written there persist into all subsequent Bash commands Claude Code runs in the session. Available only to SessionStart, Setup, CwdChanged, and FileChanged hooks — no other hook types get it.

nodes.label: Path placeholders
nodes.rationale: ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} (project root), ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} (plugin install dir, changes on each update), and ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} (persistent plugin data surviving updates) reference hook scripts regardless of working directory; both exec and shell form also export them as environment variables on the spawned process. Plugin hooks additionally substitute ${user_config.*} in exec form only — a shell-form reference to it errors instead of running.

nodes.label: Matching MCP tools
nodes.rationale: MCP tools appear as regular tools named mcp__<server>__<tool>; matching every tool of a server REQUIRES the trailing .* — a bare 'mcp__memory' contains only exact-match characters and matches no tool. Plugin-bundled servers use scoped names mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>, so a matcher against the bare server key never fires for them.

nodes.label: Hooks in skill/agent frontmatter
nodes.rationale: Skills and subagents can define hooks in YAML frontmatter, scoped to the component's lifetime and cleaned up when it finishes; 'once: true' is honored only in skill frontmatter. Since v2.1.218 frontmatter hooks in a project subagent run only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted — before that they could run from untrusted folders.

nodes.label: Hook security best practices
nodes.rationale: Command hooks execute with the user's full permissions and can modify, delete, or access anything the account can. Best practices: validate and sanitize inputs, always quote shell variables, block '..' path traversal, use absolute paths, and skip sensitive files like .env and .git/.

nodes.label: Common hook input fields
nodes.rationale: All events receive session_id, transcript_path (written asynchronously — it may lag the current turn, so Stop/SubagentStop hooks should read last_assistant_message instead), cwd, and hook_event_name; many receive permission_mode (the Manual mode arrives as 'default'), prompt_id (v2.1.196+, correlates with OpenTelemetry), and effort. Subagent calls add agent_id/agent_type; OTEL_* exporter variables are stripped from every spawned subprocess, and there is no $CLAUDE_MODEL variable.

nodes.label: /goal command
nodes.rationale: /goal is a built-in shortcut for a session-scoped prompt-based Stop hook: Claude keeps working until a condition holds, without writing hook configuration by hand.

nodes.label: SessionStart event
nodes.rationale: Fires when a session begins or resumes; matcher = startup/resume/clear/compact/fork (forks reported as 'resume' before v2.1.214). Supports only command and mcp_tool hook types; stdout is context Claude sees, and JSON can return additionalContext, initialUserMessage (creates the first turn in -p mode), sessionTitle, watchPaths, and reloadSkills (re-scan skill dirs so hook-installed skills work in the same session).

nodes.label: Setup event
nodes.rationale: Fires only with --init-only, or with --init/--maintenance combined with -p (matcher init/maintenance) — one-time preparation for CI/scripts, not per-session init. Cannot block; only command and mcp_tool types; plain stdout goes to the debug log so context must use additionalContext. Because it doesn't fire on every launch, plugins should check-and-install dependencies on first use rather than rely on Setup.

nodes.label: InstructionsLoaded event
nodes.rationale: Fires when a CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/*.md file is loaded into context — at session start and on lazy loads (matcher on load_reason: session_start, nested_traversal, path_glob_match, include, compact). Runs asynchronously for observability; no blocking or decision control.

nodes.label: UserPromptSubmit event
nodes.rationale: Fires on prompt submission before Claude processes it; can block and erase the prompt, add context via plain stdout or additionalContext, or set sessionTitle — but can never replace the prompt text. A hook that reaches its (30s default) timeout is canceled and its output INCLUDING additionalContext is discarded while the prompt proceeds without it; v2.1.196+ shows a transcript notice.

nodes.label: UserPromptExpansion event
nodes.rationale: Fires when a user-typed command expands into a prompt (expansion_type slash_command or mcp_prompt), matching on command_name; can block the expansion or add context. It covers the path PreToolUse misses: typing /skillname directly bypasses PreToolUse Skill-tool hooks entirely.

nodes.label: MessageDisplay event
nodes.rationale: Runs while assistant text streams, once per batch of newly completed lines (once per whole message in -p/Agent SDK runs, with index 0 and final true); returns displayContent to replace the rendered text. Display-only: the transcript and what Claude sees keep the original. 10s default timeout; on failure the original text is shown. Use final, not a non-empty delta, as the end-of-message signal.

nodes.label: PreToolUse event
nodes.rationale: Fires after Claude creates tool parameters and before the call runs; matches on tool name. Does NOT fire for files @-referenced in a prompt (inserted with no tool call — use a Read deny rule to block those) nor for EndConversation. File-tool file_path input is always absolute with native separators, so Windows hooks must normalize backslashes before comparing.

nodes.label: PermissionRequest event
nodes.rationale: Fires when Claude Code is about to ask for permission (vs PreToolUse, which fires on every call). A hook returns decision.behavior allow/deny, optionally with updatedInput, updatedPermissions (addRules/replaceRules/removeRules/setMode/addDirectories with destination session/localSettings/projectSettings/userSettings), message, or interrupt; an 'allow' never overrides a matching deny rule, and echoing a permission_suggestions entry equals the user clicking 'always allow'.

nodes.label: PermissionDenied event
nodes.rationale: Fires only when the auto-mode classifier denies a tool call — not on manual dialog denials, PreToolUse blocks, or deny rules. Exit code and stderr are ignored because the denial already happened; the only honored output is hookSpecificOutput.retry:true, which tells the model it may retry (the denial itself is not reversed). Prompt/agent hooks run here but their output is discarded.

nodes.label: PostToolUse event
nodes.rationale: Fires immediately after a tool completes successfully, receiving tool_input, the tool's structured tool_response, and duration_ms (excluding permission prompts and PreToolUse hooks). decision 'block' adds the reason next to the result while Claude still sees the original output; exit 2 can't block since the tool already ran, but shows stderr to Claude — useful for surfacing warnings.

nodes.label: PostToolUseFailure event
nodes.rationale: Fires when a tool that started executing fails; it does NOT fire for calls rejected before execution (unknown tool, schema validation, permission denial). Receives error, is_interrupt, duration_ms; key on tool_name, is_interrupt, and the 'Exit code N' first line and treat the rest of the error string as display text, not a stable format. Cannot block; can add additionalContext.

nodes.label: PostToolBatch event
nodes.rationale: Fires exactly once after a full batch of parallel tool calls resolves, before the next model call — the right place for context that depends on the SET of tools rather than any single one. tool_calls carries the serialized tool_result content the model sees (unlike PostToolUse's structured Output object); decision 'block' or continue:false stops the agentic loop before the next model call. No matcher.

nodes.label: Notification event
nodes.rationale: Fires when Claude Code sends a notification; matcher = type: permission_prompt, idle_prompt, auth_success, elicitation_dialog/complete/response, and agent_needs_input/agent_completed (v2.1.198+, only while agent view is open). Side effects only — cannot block or modify the notification.

nodes.label: SubagentStart event
nodes.rationale: Fires when a subagent is spawned via the Agent tool; matches on agent type (frontmatter name for custom agents; plugin agents use plugin-scoped names like my-plugin:reviewer, whose colon forces the regex path — anchor ^...$). Cannot block creation but can inject additionalContext into the subagent's conversation before its first prompt.

nodes.label: SubagentStop event
nodes.rationale: Fires when a subagent finishes; receives agent_transcript_path (the subagent's own transcript under subagents/), last_assistant_message, and parent-scoped background_tasks/session_crons (v2.1.145+). decision 'block' keeps the subagent running with reason as its next instruction; to inject context into the PARENT after a subagent returns, use a PostToolUse hook on the Agent tool instead.

nodes.label: TaskCreated event
nodes.rationale: Fires when a task is created via TaskCreate; exit 2 rolls back the creation with stderr fed to the model (e.g. enforcing subject naming conventions), while JSON continue:false stops the teammate entirely. No matcher support.

nodes.label: TaskCompleted event
nodes.rationale: Fires when a task is being marked completed — via explicit TaskUpdate, or when an agent-team teammate finishes its turn with in-progress tasks. Exit 2 prevents completion with stderr as feedback (enforce completion criteria like passing tests); continue:false stops the teammate. No matcher support.

nodes.label: Stop event
nodes.rationale: Fires when the main agent finishes responding (not on user interrupt; API errors fire StopFailure instead). Input includes stop_hook_active (check it to avoid blocking on a condition that never resolves — Claude Code overrides after 8 consecutive blocks), last_assistant_message, and background_tasks/session_crons (v2.1.145+) to distinguish 'done' from 'paused awaiting background work'. decision 'block'+reason forces continuation; hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext gives non-error continue feedback labeled 'Stop hook feedback'.

nodes.label: StopFailure event
nodes.rationale: Fires instead of Stop when the turn ends on an API error; matcher = error type (rate_limit, overloaded, authentication_failed, oauth_org_not_allowed, billing_error, invalid_request, model_not_found, server_error, max_output_tokens, unknown). Output and exit code are ignored — logging/alerting only; last_assistant_message carries the API error string itself.

nodes.label: TeammateIdle event
nodes.rationale: Fires when an agent-team teammate is about to go idle after its turn; exit 2 feeds stderr back and keeps it working — a quality-gate point (lint passing, output files exist) — while continue:false stops the teammate entirely. No matcher support.

nodes.label: ConfigChange event
nodes.rationale: Fires when a configuration file changes mid-session; matcher = source: user_settings, project_settings, local_settings, policy_settings, skills. Exit 2 or decision 'block' prevents the change from applying to the running session — EXCEPT policy_settings, whose blocking decisions are ignored so enterprise-managed settings always take effect (audit logging still works).

nodes.label: CwdChanged event
nodes.rationale: Fires when the working directory changes (e.g. Claude runs cd); no matcher, cannot block. Receives old_cwd/new_cwd and can return watchPaths to replace the dynamic FileChanged watch list (empty array clears it); pairs with FileChanged for direnv-style reactive environment management.

nodes.label: DirectoryAdded event
nodes.rationale: Fires after a working directory is added mid-session via /add-dir or the SDK register_repo_root (NOT for --add-dir at startup — SessionStart covers those), after sandbox/permission state has refreshed. Cannot block; uniquely, for slash_command adds the hook's systemMessage is delivered to Claude as context on the next turn instead of to the user.

nodes.label: FileChanged event
nodes.rationale: Fires when a watched file changes on disk (event: change/add/unlink). Its matcher plays two roles: split on '|' as LITERAL filenames to build the watch list (a regex like ^\.env would watch a file literally named that), then as a standard matcher filtering which hook groups run against the changed file's basename. watchPaths output (also from SessionStart and CwdChanged) extends the watch list dynamically.

nodes.label: WorktreeCreate event
nodes.rationale: Fires when a worktree is created (--worktree, subagent isolation:'worktree', or a background session) and REPLACES the default git-worktree behavior, enabling SVN/Perforce/Mercurial; .worktreeinclude is then not processed. The hook must return the created path (last non-empty stdout line for command hooks, hookSpecificOutput.worktreePath for HTTP); any non-zero exit or missing path fails creation. Since v2.1.216 absolute paths containing ./.. segments or passing through a symlink below the repo root are refused.

nodes.label: WorktreeRemove event
nodes.rationale: The cleanup counterpart to WorktreeCreate: fires when a worktree is removed at session exit, when a worktree-isolated subagent finishes, or when a background session is deleted; receives worktree_path (the path WorktreeCreate returned). No decision control; failures are logged in debug mode only; the stored path is symlink-screened before the hook runs (v2.1.216+).

nodes.label: PreCompact event
nodes.rationale: Fires before context compaction; matcher manual (/compact, with custom_instructions) or auto. Exit 2 or decision 'block' blocks compaction — blocking a proactive auto-compact just skips it and the conversation continues, but blocking a compaction that was recovering from a context-limit error lets the underlying error surface and the request fails.

nodes.label: PostCompact event
nodes.rationale: Fires after a compact operation completes (matcher manual/auto); receives compact_summary containing the generated conversation summary. No decision control — for reacting to the new compacted state, e.g. logging the summary.

nodes.label: SessionEnd event
nodes.rationale: Fires when a session terminates; matcher = reason: clear, resume (interactive /resume switch), logout, prompt_input_exit, bypass_permissions_disabled, other. Cannot block termination; used for cleanup and logging, and runs under the tight shared 1.5-second hook budget.

nodes.label: Elicitation event
nodes.rationale: Fires when an MCP server requests user input mid-tool-call (form mode with requested_schema, or url mode for browser auth); matcher = MCP server name. A hook can respond programmatically with action accept/decline/cancel plus content (form values), skipping the dialog entirely; exit 2 denies the elicitation.

nodes.label: ElicitationResult event
nodes.rationale: Fires after the user responds to an MCP elicitation, before the response is sent back to the server; matcher = MCP server name. Hooks can observe, override action/content, or block — exit 2 blocks the response and changes the effective action to decline.

nodes.label: Skill
nodes.rationale: Skills extend what Claude can do in Claude Code: a SKILL.md file with instructions is added to Claude's toolkit, used automatically when relevant or invoked directly with /skill-name. Create one when the same instructions or multi-step procedure keeps being pasted into chat; unlike CLAUDE.md content, a skill's body loads only when used, so long reference material costs almost nothing until needed.

nodes.label: SKILL.md entrypoint
nodes.rationale: Every skill is a directory whose required entrypoint is SKILL.md: YAML frontmatter between --- markers that tells Claude when to use the skill, plus markdown instructions Claude follows when it runs. Keep it under 500 lines and concise — once loaded, its content stays in context across turns, so every line is a recurring token cost.

nodes.label: Custom commands (.claude/commands/)
nodes.rationale: Custom commands have been merged into skills: .claude/commands/deploy.md and .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md both create /deploy and work the same way. Existing .claude/commands/ files keep working and support the same frontmatter; skills add supporting files, invocation control, and automatic loading. If a skill and a command share a name, the skill takes precedence.

nodes.label: Agent Skills open standard
nodes.rationale: Claude Code skills follow the Agent Skills open standard (agentskills.io), which works across multiple AI tools. Claude Code extends the standard with additional features like invocation control, subagent execution, and dynamic context injection.

nodes.label: Bundled skills
nodes.rationale: Claude Code ships bundled skills such as /doctor, /code-review, /batch, /debug, /loop, and /claude-api. They are prompt-based — detailed instructions Claude orchestrates with its tools — unlike most built-in commands, which execute fixed logic. Available in every session; since v2.1.215, /verify and /code-review run only when the user invokes them (before that Claude could run them on its own).

nodes.label: disableBundledSkills setting
nodes.rationale: The disableBundledSkills setting disables every bundled skill except /doctor. /doctor stays typable when the setting is on (v2.1.205+, when /doctor became a bundled skill rather than a built-in command); hide it with the DISABLE_DOCTOR_COMMAND environment variable or a skillOverrides entry of doctor: off.

nodes.label: /run bundled skill
nodes.rationale: /run launches and drives your app to see a change working. It works without setup by inferring the launch from project type (CLI, server, TUI, browser-driven) and from README, package.json, or Makefile; that inference gets unreliable for projects needing anything beyond a standard launch. Requires Claude Code v2.1.145 or later.

nodes.label: /verify bundled skill
nodes.rationale: /verify builds and runs your app to confirm a code change does what it should, without falling back to tests or type checks. Since v2.1.200 it can record its own recipe to .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md (at the repo root the recorded skill replaces the bundled /verify); since v2.1.205 Claude edits the recorded file only when it steered a run wrong, so it can be committed without per-session diffs.

nodes.label: /run-skill-generator
nodes.rationale: /run-skill-generator records the launch recipe: it gets the app running from a clean environment, captures what worked (install commands, env vars, launch script), and commits it as a per-project skill at .claude/skills/run-<name>/. After that, /run, /verify, and any other agent in the repo follow the recorded recipe instead of rediscovering it. Run once per project, again if the build or launch process changes.

nodes.label: Skill storage levels
nodes.rationale: Where a skill is stored determines who can use it: Enterprise (managed settings, all org users), Personal (~/.claude/skills/, all your projects), Project (.claude/skills/, this project only), Plugin (<plugin>/skills/, where the plugin is enabled). On a shared name, enterprise overrides personal and personal overrides project; a skill at any level also overrides a bundled skill with the same name.

nodes.label: Nested skill directories
nodes.rationale: Skills also load from nested .claude/skills/ directories below the working directory. They are not loaded at startup: they load the first time Claude reads or edits a file inside that subdirectory and stay available for the rest of the session — letting a monorepo package provide its own skills that apply when working on that package. Until loaded, they don't appear in autocomplete and can't be invoked by name.

nodes.label: Directory-qualified skill name
nodes.rationale: If a nested skill shares a name with another skill, both stay available: the nested one appears under a directory-qualified name such as apps/web:deploy, its description says which directory it applies to, and Claude picks the variant matching the files it is working on. Typing /deploy runs the project-root skill; typing the qualified /apps/web:deploy runs the nested variant explicitly.

nodes.label: Unqualified invocation appends variant list
nodes.rationale: When you or Claude invoke the unqualified name, the project-root skill loads and Claude Code appends a list of the directory-qualified variants to its content with an instruction to also invoke any variant whose directory holds the files Claude is working on. A nested skill therefore still applies to work in its directory when only the unqualified name is invoked. Requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later.

nodes.label: Plugin skill namespace
nodes.rationale: Plugin skills use a plugin-name:skill-name namespace, so they cannot conflict with skills at other levels. In a plugin skill the frontmatter name sets the last segment of the command while the plugin prefix stays in place (v2.1.216+; before that the frontmatter name replaced the whole command name, so /my-plugin:fancy didn't autocomplete). The bare /fancy also invokes the skill unless another command already uses that name.

nodes.label: Symlinked skill entries
nodes.rationale: A <skill-name> entry in the enterprise, personal, or project locations can be a symlink to a directory elsewhere on disk. Claude Code follows the symlink and reads SKILL.md from the target directory, and if the same target is reachable from more than one location, the skill loads once. Plugin skills handle symlinks differently (marketplace symlink sharing).

nodes.label: Live change detection
nodes.rationale: Claude Code watches skill directories: adding, editing, or removing a skill under ~/.claude/skills/, the project .claude/skills/, or a .claude/skills/ inside an --add-dir directory is picked up within the current session, without a restart. Coverage is SKILL.md text only — a skill folder that is also a plugin needs /reload-plugins for changes to hooks/, .mcp.json, agents/, and output-styles/. A brand-new top-level skills directory needs a restart to be watched.

nodes.label: --add-dir skill loading exception
nodes.rationale: --add-dir and /add-dir grant file access rather than configuration discovery, but skills are an exception: .claude/skills/ within an added directory is loaded automatically. The permissions.additionalDirectories setting grants file access only and does not load skills, and other .claude/ configuration such as commands and output styles is not loaded from additional directories.

nodes.label: Skills in Cowork and cloud sessions
nodes.rationale: Cowork sessions and cloud sessions (including routines) don't read ~/.claude/skills/ on your machine: they load the skills enabled for your claude.ai account, synced at session start, and cloud sessions additionally load project skills committed to the cloned repo's .claude/skills/ or shipped in a repo-declared plugin. A personal skill that exists only locally is reported not found when a routine invokes it. Desktop scheduled tasks are different: they run locally and load skills from the same locations as any local session.

nodes.label: SKILL.md YAML frontmatter
nodes.rationale: Skill behavior is configured through YAML frontmatter fields at the top of SKILL.md: name, description, when_to_use, argument-hint, arguments, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, allowed-tools, disallowed-tools, model, effort, context, agent, background, hooks, paths, shell, metadata, license, and compatibility. All fields are optional; only description is recommended. Boolean fields accept yes/no/on/off/1/0 in any letter case in addition to true/false since v2.1.218.

nodes.label: description frontmatter field
nodes.rationale: The description states what the skill does and when to use it; Claude uses it to decide when to apply the skill automatically. If omitted, the first paragraph of the markdown content is used. Put the key use case first: the combined description and when_to_use text is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing to reduce context usage.

nodes.label: disable-model-invocation field
nodes.rationale: disable-model-invocation: true means only the user can invoke the skill — for workflows with side effects or timing control like /commit, /deploy, /send-slack-message. It removes the skill's description from context entirely, prevents preloading into subagents, and as of v2.1.196 prevents the skill from running when a scheduled task fires with it as the prompt. If Claude tries anyway, Claude Code blocks the call and instructs it not to reproduce the steps another way.

nodes.label: user-invocable: false field
nodes.rationale: user-invocable: false hides a skill from the / menu so only Claude can invoke it — for background knowledge that isn't actionable as a command (e.g. a legacy-system-context skill). It controls menu visibility only, not Skill tool access; use disable-model-invocation: true to block programmatic invocation.

nodes.label: allowed-tools frontmatter field
nodes.rationale: allowed-tools grants permission for the listed tools during the turn that invokes the skill, so Claude can use them without prompting. The grant clears when the user sends the next message, even though the skill content stays in context; re-invoking re-applies it for that turn. It does not restrict which tools are available. For project skills it takes effect only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted — review project skills before trusting a repository, since a skill can grant itself broad tool access.

nodes.label: disallowed-tools frontmatter field
nodes.rationale: disallowed-tools removes the listed tools from Claude's available pool while the skill is active — for autonomous skills that should never call certain tools, such as AskUserQuestion in a background loop. The restriction clears when the user sends the next message, and like deny rules the field can't remove EndConversation while any other tool remains.

nodes.label: model frontmatter field
nodes.rationale: The model field selects a model to use while the skill is active; the override applies for the rest of the current turn and is not saved to settings — the session model resumes on the next prompt. Accepts the same values as /model, or 'inherit'. A value excluded by the organization's availableModels allowlist is not used and the session keeps its current model.

nodes.label: context: fork (forked subagent skill)
nodes.rationale: context: fork runs a skill in an isolated forked subagent whose prompt is the skill content; it has no access to conversation history, so it only makes sense for skills with explicit task instructions — guideline-only content returns without meaningful output. The fork runs in the background by default (before v2.1.218 forked skills always blocked the turn), but Claude Code waits anyway in non-interactive mode, when CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1, when an earlier invocation of the same skill is still running, or when a scheduled task fires the skill.

nodes.label: agent frontmatter field
nodes.rationale: The agent field picks which subagent configuration executes a context: fork skill — built-in Explore, Plan, general-purpose, or any custom subagent from .claude/agents/; general-purpose if omitted. The agent type determines model, tools, and permissions. Explore and Plan skip CLAUDE.md and git status to keep context small, so a forked skill with agent: Explore sees only the SKILL.md content and the agent's own system prompt.

nodes.label: background frontmatter field
nodes.rationale: background: false makes a forked skill wait for the subagent's result in the turn that invoked it, instead of running in the background. Only applies with context: fork; default is true; requires Claude Code v2.1.218 or later.

nodes.label: Background fork tool-set restriction
nodes.rationale: A backgrounded fork runs with the narrower tool set that applies to background subagents — the skill's subagent is a regular agent type, so the exemption for subagents that fork the conversation doesn't cover it. Its edits also apply outside the session's checkpoints, so /rewind doesn't undo them; use git to revert. If the skill's steps depend on a tool outside that set, set background: false to keep the full tool set.

nodes.label: paths frontmatter field
nodes.rationale: The paths field takes glob patterns that limit when the skill is activated: when set, Claude loads the skill automatically only when working with files matching the patterns. Uses the same format as path-specific memory rules.

nodes.label: metadata frontmatter field
nodes.rationale: metadata is a free-form YAML map for the author's own key-value data, such as entitlement or catalog fields, read by external tooling from SKILL.md. Claude Code doesn't act on its contents and drops a value that isn't a map. Don't reuse frontmatter field names such as paths as keys.

nodes.label: Agent Skills spec frontmatter fields
nodes.rationale: Outside Claude Code — claude.ai skill uploads, the Skills API, and packaging with package_skill.py — only the Agent Skills spec's six frontmatter fields are usable: name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools. Including any other field fails packaging or upload with a hard error rather than being ignored. Claude Code accepts all six, so spec-conforming frontmatter loads in Claude Code without changes.

nodes.label: Skill command-name derivation
nodes.rationale: The command you type comes from where the skill file lives: the directory name for ~/.claude/skills/ and .claude/skills/, a subdirectory-path-qualified name for clashing nested skills, the file name for .claude/commands/, and plugin-namespaced names for plugin skills where frontmatter name sets the last segment (or the whole final segment for a plugin-root SKILL.md). In personal or project skills, the frontmatter name sets only the display label shown in listings.

nodes.label: Skill string substitutions
nodes.rationale: Skill content supports substitutions: $ARGUMENTS (full argument string, appended as 'ARGUMENTS: <value>' if absent from content), $ARGUMENTS[N] and $N (0-based positional), $name (named via the arguments frontmatter list), ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}, ${CLAUDE_EFFORT}, ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}, and ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} (v2.1.196+). Indexed arguments use shell-style quoting; an unmatched indexed placeholder stays unchanged while an unmatched named placeholder expands to empty; a single backslash escapes a literal $ before a token.

nodes.label: ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} variable
nodes.rationale: ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} expands to the directory containing the skill's SKILL.md — for plugin skills, the skill's subdirectory within the plugin, not the plugin root — so bundled scripts resolve regardless of the current working directory or install level. It is substituted in both the markdown content and Bash rules in allowed-tools; the allowed-tools substitution requires v2.1.129+ (earlier versions leave a literal string that never matches, so the command still prompts).

nodes.label: Skill supporting files
nodes.rationale: A skill directory can hold files beyond SKILL.md — templates, example outputs, scripts, detailed reference docs — that don't load into context every time the skill runs, keeping SKILL.md focused on essentials. Reference them from SKILL.md so Claude knows what each file contains and when to load it; scripts are executed, not loaded.

nodes.label: Skill content lifecycle
nodes.rationale: When a skill is invoked, the rendered SKILL.md content enters the conversation as a single message and stays there for the rest of the session; Claude Code does not re-read the file on later turns, so guidance should be written as standing instructions. Since v2.1.202, re-invoking a skill whose rendered content is identical adds a short already-loaded note instead of a second copy; if arguments or dynamic-context output changed, the full content is appended again.

nodes.label: Auto-compaction skill budget
nodes.rationale: Auto-compaction carries invoked skills forward within a token budget: after summarization, Claude Code re-attaches the most recent invocation of each skill, keeping the first 5,000 tokens of each within a combined 25,000-token budget filled from the most recently invoked skill — so older skills can be dropped entirely. Re-invoke a skill after compaction to restore its full content.

nodes.label: Dynamic context injection
nodes.rationale: The !`command` syntax runs shell commands before the skill content is sent to Claude; the output replaces the placeholder so Claude receives actual data, not the command. This is preprocessing, not something Claude executes. Substitution runs once over the original file — output is not re-scanned for further placeholders; the inline form is recognized only at line start or after whitespace; multi-line commands use a ```! fenced block; a shell frontmatter field can switch inline commands to PowerShell.

nodes.label: disableSkillShellExecution setting
nodes.rationale: Setting disableSkillShellExecution: true disables !`command` execution for skills and custom commands from user, project, plugin, or additional-directory sources: each command is replaced with '[shell command execution disabled by policy]' instead of being run. Bundled and managed skills are not affected. Most useful in managed settings, where users cannot override it.

nodes.label: Skill stacking
nodes.rationale: Several skills can be stacked at the start of one message (v2.1.199+; before that only the first loaded): Claude Code expands the first skill plus up to five more, and the trailing text becomes the argument text for every expanded skill. Expansion stops at the first token that isn't an inline user-invocable skill — a skill that runs as a forked subagent, such as /code-review (forked from v2.1.218), or one whose arguments may start with a slash command, such as /loop, ends the run there.

nodes.label: Skill permission rules
nodes.rationale: Which skills Claude can invoke is controlled through permission rules: deny the Skill tool to disable all skills, or use Skill(name) for exact match and Skill(name *) for prefix match with any arguments to allow or deny specific skills. A few built-in commands (/init, /review, /security-review) are also available through the Skill tool; others such as /compact are not.

nodes.label: skillOverrides setting
nodes.rationale: skillOverrides controls skill visibility from settings instead of the skill's own frontmatter — useful for skills checked into a shared repo whose SKILL.md you don't want to edit. Four states per skill: on (name and description listed), name-only, user-invocable-only (hidden from Claude but in the / menu), and off (hidden everywhere; since v2.1.199 also hidden from Remote Control and Agent SDK command lists). The /skills menu writes it to .claude/settings.local.json. Plugin skills are not affected — manage those through /plugin.

nodes.label: Skill evaluation by baseline comparison
nodes.rationale: Seeing a skill trigger only shows Claude found it, not that it did what you intended. Measure two things separately: whether Claude invokes it on the prompts it should, and whether the output matches expectations when it does. The check for both is a baseline comparison: run realistic prompts in a fresh session with the skill available and again with it disabled, and compare — a fresh session matters because leftover authoring context masks gaps in the written instructions.

nodes.label: skill-creator plugin evals
nodes.rationale: The skill-creator plugin (from the claude-plugins-official marketplace) automates the skill-comparison loop inside Claude Code: test cases stored in evals.json in the skill directory, isolated per-case subagent runs recording tokens and duration, assertion grading into grading.json, with-skill vs without-skill benchmarking into benchmark.json, blind A/B version comparison, description tuning via should-trigger/should-not-trigger prompts, and an HTML review viewer for qualitative feedback.

nodes.label: Skill listing character budget
nodes.rationale: The skill listing loaded into context always contains every skill name, but with many skills Claude Code shortens descriptions to fit a character budget that scales at 1% of the model's context window, dropping descriptions starting with the least-invoked skills. Raise it with skillListingBudgetFraction (e.g. 0.02) or the SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET env var; the per-entry 1,536-character cap is configurable with skillListingMaxDescChars. /doctor estimates the listing's cost; the /context Skills row reports the post-budget size (v2.1.196+).

nodes.label: Malformed frontmatter fallback
nodes.rationale: If the frontmatter YAML is malformed, Claude Code loads the skill body with empty metadata: /skill-name still works, but Claude has no description to match against, so automatic invocation fails. Run with --debug to see the parse error.
